text:
jess: cloudsec-bot flagged a GitHub Actions secret in infra repo named `CI_SA_KEY` that contains a service account key with project-level Owner. possible accidental checkin. need immediate containment.
cloudsec-bot: detection: service-account-key-leak in repo `infra/configs` — alert created (id: cs-2026-179). auto-cc @eng-security.
mike: on it. containment plan: 1) remove GH secret, 2) delete/disable SA key, 3) remove Owner binding, 4) rotate any dependent keys. i'll take 1-2 now.
nana: (typo) ana: also check cloud audit logs for any unusual `storage.objects.get` or IAM changes. if exfil happened we need timeline + IPs.
sofia: running quick log query to look for activity: `gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"" --limit 100` — will paste results.
devops: commands i'm executing now:
```
# list service account keys
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# delete compromised key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --quiet
# remove project Owner binding
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/owner
```
mike: removed GH secret from repo, deleted key KEY_ID, and revoked Owner role. downgraded SA to minimal runtime role for CI: `roles/run.invoker` for the short term. :lock:
tom: good containment. legal/trust aware? @ana please loop them in and prepare initial incident notice if customer-facing data involved.
nana: ana: creating incident timeline doc: https://docs.internal/incident/INC-2026-45 — adding detection logs and containment steps. question: that SA was used by CI to access encrypted buckets — did it have KMS cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter? need to audit KMS IAM bindings.
sofia: quick audit shows some `storage.objects.get` on `staging-artifacts` between 02:10-02:25 UTC by that SA, and a few `kms.cryptoKeyVersions.access` attempts to `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/artifacts`. no obvious external transfers yet. exporting full logs for retention.
devops: applied temporary org-level deny policy for that SA to prevent outgoing egress while we investigate: `gcloud organizations set-iam-policy ORG_ID deny-policy.yaml` — will revert after rotation.
mike: follow-ups: (a) rotate any KMS keys if SA had decryption perms, (b) remove long-lived SA keys and switch GH actions to workload identity federation, (c) add repo secret blocking and pre-commit scan. i'll open PRs and tickets.
jess: thanks team. post-incident action items for postmortem: enforce least-privilege on CI accounts, remove long-lived keys, enable VPC Service Controls for sensitive buckets, require key rotation cadence, add audit alerting for service-account secrets in repos. assign owners and ETA in the incident doc.
cloudsec-bot: incident cs-2026-179 set to CONTAINED by mike at 1764127410. follow-ups assigned: CS-179-1 (rotate KMS keys), CS-179-2 (workload identity rollout), CS-179-3 (repo secret scanning).
